results.name: Dumbbell Figure Four Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and place a dumbbell across your hips. Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor, then cross one ankle over the opposite knee in a figure four position.
Press through the heel of your grounded foot to lift your hips upward in a swift motion, extending your hips until your torso forms a straight line from your shoulders to your bent knee.
At the peak of the movement, squeeze your glutes and hold the position for a second. Lower your hips back down with control until they lightly touch the floor.
Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Make sure the bench is stable and positioned at mid-back level for proper support.
Place the dumbbell securely on your hips and use your hands to hold it in place throughout the movement.
Keep your core tight to prevent lower back arching and maintain pelvic stability.
results.description: Dumbbell Figure Four Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Frog Jumps
instructions: Bend your knees and lower into a deep squat while keeping your chest up, with your feet wider than shoulder-width, holding a dumbbell in each hand hanging between your legs.
Push through your heels and extend your legs to stand upright, bringing the dumbbells to your sides.
Explosively jump straight up from the squat position, extending through your hips, knees, and ankles.
Land softly back into the squat position with control and immediately go into the next rep.
tips: Use explosive power from your legs to jump up.
Land with soft knees to reduce impact on joints.
Engage your core throughout the movement.
results.description: Dumbbell Frog Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Abdominals, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Dumbbell Goblet Forward Lunge
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands, elbows pointing down.
Take a step forward with one leg and begin descending by bending both knees.
Descend until your front thigh is parallel to the ground and your back knee is just above the floor.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position, then repeat on the opposite leg.
tips: Ensure your front knee stays aligned with your foot and does not travel past your toes.
Engage your core muscles for added stability during the lunge.
Hold the dumbbell close to your chest to maintain proper posture and balance.
results.description: Dumbbell Goblet Forward Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Dumbbell Goblet Reverse Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands.
Step one foot backward and bend both knees, lowering your back knee toward the floor.
Keep your chest up and your front foot flat as you lower into the lunge.
Push through your front foot to return to standing, then repeat with the opposite leg.
tips: Step far enough back to maintain a stable lunge position.
Align your front knee with your toes.
Avoid pushing off excessively with your back foot as you stand.
Inhale as you lower and exhale as you return to standing.
results.description: Dumbbell Goblet Reverse Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Offset Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell against your shoulder with a neutral grip. Extend your opposite arm forward at shoulder height for balance.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat while keeping your chest lifted and your torso facing forward.
Lower until your thighs are approximately parallel to the floor, or as far as you can while keeping your heels down and your knees aligned with your toes.
Press through your heels to stand upright, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions before holding the dumbbell on the opposite side.
tips: Brace your core to prevent your torso from leaning toward the weighted side.
Keep your hips and shoulders level without twisting your body.
Distribute your weight evenly across your heels and the middle of your feet.
Inhale as you lower into the squat and exhale as you return to standing.
results.description: Dumbbell Offset Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core, Obliques.

results.name: Dumbbell Single Leg Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against the edge of a flat bench. Plant one foot firmly on the floor, extend the opposite leg straight in front of you, and hold a dumbbell securely across your hips with both hands.
Press through your planted foot and extend your hips upward while keeping the opposite leg straight and elevated.
Lift until your torso and supporting thigh form a straight line, then pause briefly and squeeze your glutes.
Slowly lower your hips toward the floor while keeping the extended leg raised, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your upper back firmly supported against the bench throughout the movement.
Drive through the heel and middle of your planted foot rather than your toes.
Keep your hips level and avoid rotating toward the raised leg.
Inhale as you lower your hips and exhale as you press them upward.
results.description: Dumbbell Single Leg Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core, Obliques.

results.name: Dumbbell Single Leg Single Arm Deadlift
instructions: Stand upright with your feet together and hold a dumbbell by your side using a neutral grip. Shift your weight onto the leg opposite the dumbbell and slightly bend your supporting knee.
Lift the leg on the dumbbell side behind you with your knee bent as you push your hips back and hinge your torso forward.
Lower the dumbbell toward the floor beside your supporting leg until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight and your hips level.
Press through your supporting foot and drive your hips forward to return upright, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Lower the dumbbell close to your supporting leg instead of reaching it forward.
Keep your supporting knee aligned with your toes and balance over the middle of your foot.
Keep your hips level and avoid rotating your torso toward either side.
Inhale as you hinge forward and exhale as you return to standing.
results.description: Dumbbell Single Leg Single Arm Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Obliques, Lower Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Staggered Deadlift
instructions: Stand with one foot fully planted and place the opposite foot a short step behind, resting on the ball of the foot with the heel raised. Hold a dumbbell in each hand using an overhand grip.
Shift most of your weight onto the front leg, slightly bend both knees, and push your hips backward as you hinge your torso forward.
Lower the dumbbells in front of your shins while keeping your back straight and the weights close to your legs.
Press through your front foot and drive your hips forward to return upright, then complete the repetitions before switching your stance.
tips: Keep most of your body weight on the front leg and use the rear foot mainly for balance.
Push your hips backward rather than lowering into a squat.
Stop lowering when you feel a controlled stretch without rounding your back.
Inhale as you hinge forward and exhale as you return to standing.
results.description: Dumbbell Staggered Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Staggered Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and hold a dumbbell securely across your hips. Plant one foot close to your hips and place the opposite heel slightly farther forward with the toes raised.
Press primarily through the foot closest to your hips while using the forward heel lightly for balance.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees, keeping your hips level.
Pause and squeeze your glutes, then lower your hips with control and complete the repetitions before switching to the other side.
tips: Keep the foot closest to your hips firmly planted throughout the movement.
Use the forward heel mainly for balance rather than pushing equally through both legs.
Drive through the heel and middle of your working foot rather than your toes.
Inhale as you lower your hips and exhale as you lift them.
results.description: Dumbbell Staggered Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Staggered Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit with your upper back against the edge of a flat bench and hold a dumbbell securely across your hips. Plant one foot close to your hips and place the opposite heel slightly farther forward with the toes raised.
Press primarily through the foot closest to your hips and lift your hips toward the ceiling while using the forward heel lightly for balance.
Continue lifting until your torso and working thigh form a straight line, keeping your hips level and squeezing your glutes at the top.
Lower your hips with control, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other side.
tips: Place most of your weight through the foot closest to your hips.
Use the farther heel mainly for balance rather than driving equally through both legs.
Stop at full hip extension without arching your lower back.
Inhale as you lower your hips and exhale as you press them upward.
results.description: Dumbbell Staggered Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core, Calves.
